decisions.decision: Separate local product repository; immutable hashed research inputs; no upstream source or asset reuse.
Use Node 22 standard-library foundation tooling, built-in tests and JSON tracking without selecting a product execution engine.
Apache-2.0 is proposed; no product license grant or public naming clearance is approved.
Preserve modular governance and restricted worker boundary. Parser, driver, locks, ledger and recovery require actual WP0 acceptance.

Pin Node22.23.3/npm10.9.9, TypeScript6.0.2, node-oracledb7.0.1 Thin, Postgres.js3.4.9; evaluate Flyway13.9.0 on Temurin21.0.12.1+1/Maven3.9.16. Exact source/artifact/license evidence exists; no proprietary driver requirement or product/distribution approval.

Driver-free Flyway packaging works, but corpus has 11 comment/SQL*Plus compatibility failures. Reject this profile for execution; T03 remains blocked until a licensed mature parser satisfies all required goldens. No custom tokenizer/grammar/splitter fallback.

Select unchanged Apache-2.0 PL/SQL grammars-v4 7df52be9 with ANTLR4.13.2 BSD runtime, reviewed project-authored hook rewrites, lossless parser-context/token byte adapter and complete-release prevalidation. Exact31file corpus and4realhelper regressions pass. External generator/JDK and separate runtime; no headerless upstream bases, custom grammar/splitter, runtime execution or product-distribution approval. This supersedes the rejected Flyway profile for offline T03 only; runtime ADR-I03/G2 requires both Oracle versions.

Development scheduling uses independent PRODUCT and VALIDATION tracks. Oracle runtime and acceptance remain VALIDATION gates; original catalog and imported work acceptance dependencies are immutable and enforced for verification.

Owner selected unmodified PolyForm Shield 1.0.0 for independently authored software/current documentation. Free internal use; competing products/services restricted; noncompeting paid support not categorically prohibited. Third-party grants and immutable research provenance retained; naming and F31 distribution closure remain pending.

Independently choose ordinary product, architecture, implementation, compatibility and migration defaults using existing requirements, security principles and engineering judgment. Select the safest reasonable default, document it, implement/test/verify and continue through eligible PR/merge. For existing data prefer explicit authorization, backward-compatible reads where safe, preserved history and documented recovery. Escalate only external credentials/permissions, financial cost, irreversible real user data loss, license/business-model changes or unresolved material security/legal risk. A safe documented default prevents a design choice alone from blocking the whole goal.

Use server-computed SHA256 digests of trusted high-entropy local bearer credentials with database-clock fixed 24-hour expiry, persisted revocation and insert-only credential seeding. Keep existing stable identities/fixed roles and immutable historical decision names. Only the trusted local OS operator rotates/revokes credentials through private files and explicit crash recovery; no application administrator or membership grant is introduced by T20. Auth applies to subsequent request admission, not cancellation of previously admitted operations. Preserve the authorized loopback UI; this is partial SEC-001, not full original WP4/Oracle acceptance.

Trusted local OS operator alone may explicitly grant/revoke project access for existing fixed developer/approver actors. Require explicit grants for all projects; establish safe operator bootstrap and recovery before enforcing deny-by-default. Do not infer owners or backfill memberships from historical audit records. Preserve project data, comments, plans, decisions, history and audits. No application administrator or Oracle execution authority is conferred. Implement after T20; registration, enforcement and verification are not yet claimed.

Apply owner SF-D012 through authenticated legacy read-only bootstrap with every project mutation denied before writes/audit, explicit local OS operator grants, atomic one-way enforcement after every existing project has usable explicit membership, no creator/audit inference or historical rewrite. Once enforced all project resources require current membership and fixed role; creation returns a pending-grant receipt only. Operator remains independent of expired/revoked API credentials for recovery. Revocation applies to subsequent request admission, consistent with T20; already-admitted operations may finish. Full original WP4/Oracle/remoteIAM excluded.

Prioritize useful approval review of parser-derived exact statement source ranges and validated execution digests after explicit membership. Recompute scoped authorized retained UTF-8 bytes with the existing pinned ANTLR helper after SQL resource bounds and retained integrity checks; preserve historical manifests/intents/plans and fixed membership/read-only/stale-response guards. No historical backfill, regex splitting, worker/execution/Oracle or full SQL015/GOV013 acceptance. Ordinary safe compatibility choice under standing SF-D010 policy.

Retained format-1 manifest excludes statementCount. Preview verifies any retained numeric count against current pinned-parser output and rejects mismatches; a historical NULL remains NULL in PostgreSQL and the read-only response reports the recomputed count. Preserve complete source/manifest/intent/history bytes and unavailable feedback. Ordinary safe read-compatibility default under SF-D010, no historical backfill or execution authority.

Prioritize supplemental server-resolved statement references in pending-plan discussion after T22. Maximum eight compact references, no uploaded SQL/blob/URL/title. Bind to exact retained format-1 intent digest/release/file/profile and recomputed statement byte/source/execution facts under existing locks; do not claim format1 includes statement hashes. Preserve body-only comments and historical reads; legacy/malformed/stale intent or generation cannot accept new evidence refs, requiring a fresh eligible plan. No worker/target/Oracle acceptance. Ordinary safest reasonable default under SF-D010.

T23 accepts at most eight strict statement descriptors, each with a retained relative file path bounded to 4096 UTF-8 bytes and the complete descriptor list bounded to 48 KiB. A 160-byte path limit would reject valid existing configured folder prefixes (up to 200 characters), so use the compatible bounded limit. Independently bound resolved stored facts before persistence; derive release, parser profile, retained source-file hash and intent digest server-side. Preserve exact existing body-only audit facts when no references are submitted. Ordinary reversible compatibility and resource limits under SF-D010; no source, historical intent or generation backfill.

Explicit T23 descriptor selections may span files of one verified immutable selected-plan release. Switching only the displayed preview file discards late preview results while preserving those explicit selections. Plan/project/release/session/token or invalidated source-context changes clear selections. Server revalidates every descriptor against fresh generation, retained intent and pinned source before persistence. This clarifies the bounded T23 draft criterion without changing original GOV-020 or 220-feature requirements; no SQL is retained in descriptors and no execution authority is added. Ordinary safe product decision under SF-D010.

Prioritize authenticated project audit keyset pagination after T23: actual current API and UI hide events older than the recent 100. Preserve the recent-window project-detail contract, add bounded descending (created_at,id) pages with exact PostgreSQL microsecond cursor facts and old-action filtering. Treat strict project/filter-bound cursors as untrusted positions, recheck current membership on every page and preserve archived reads. Add only an ordering index; no historical rewrite, search/retention/export/tamper-proof or Oracle claims. Higher coherent Database DevOps value than a summary dashboard of already reachable review state. Ordinary safe reversible priority/compatibility decision under SF-D010; original 220-feature dependencies/acceptance unchanged.

T24 adds GET /api/projects/:id/audit with a fixed page size of 50, historical project-owned exact-action choices, hasMore and nextCursor. Preserve the existing project-detail recent-100 view. Encode an untrusted exclusive query position as canonical unpadded base64url JSON with exact ordered fields {v,p,a,t,i}: version 1, project ID, action or null, exact six-digit UTC PostgreSQL timestamp and event ID. Bound and strictly validate encoding, fields, calendar/time, IDs and project/filter agreement; cursors grant no authority and current explicit membership is checked on every request. Use PostgreSQL (created_at,id) DESC and limit-plus-one, never round cursor timestamps through JavaScript Date. The only schema change is an additive scoped ordering index; existing records and audit actions remain intact. Context changes clear previously displayed page rows and cursors and discard delayed responses; users may refresh from the latest page after failure. Paging is a read view over retained events, not a frozen multi-request snapshot: newly inserted newer events appear on refresh, with no counter or retention/tamper assertion. Authorized archived reads remain available. Ordinary reversible default under SF-D010 and SF-D019; no target, Oracle or external credential authority.

The first frozen T24 browser suite exposed an actual T09 compatibility regression: alphabetical historical action choices changed the established newest-occurrence order. Preserve existing action-choice behavior across the full retained project audit set by selecting each action’s newest (created_at,id) occurrence and ordering those occurrences descending, including actions older than the recent100. Retain all original T09 assertions, immutable failure capture and timestamp/ID tie semantics; correct only the new implementation and its new expected historical-action results, then rerun the complete frozen standard/product/browser suites. This is a bounded compatibility repair under SF-D010/SF-D019/SF-D020, not a redesign or original acceptance change. No audit records, thresholds, parser logic, security gates or Oracle authority change.

After T24, prioritize a read-only comparison of two retained Git migration-release sources. The existing220 catalog and actual importer/verifier/UI expose complete immutable release identities but only one retained release at a time; pairwise source review improves release preparation without target credentials. Require current same-project membership, compatible retained repository/folder/parser-profile and bounded manifest revalidation under consistent scoped read locks before loading payloads. Align by canonical arbitrary-precision migration version and retain both paths/content/hash facts: a same-version rename is a changed source fact; self comparison is a valid unchanged source view. Preserve authorized archived and repository-unavailable reads, all historical source/intent/generation/review records and no-write semantics. Failures are retryable scoped reads; never infer a deployed baseline, raw-byte history, schema snapshots or Oracle facts. This supports MIG-008/MIG-009 as a bounded extension without altering original acceptance or dependencies; MIG-013 applied checksum enforcement, MIG-014/MIG-033 drift/schema comparison and GIT-015 deployed provenance remain unverified. Audit search is a later alternative; observed schema work still requires authorized evidence. Ordinary safe reversible priority and compatibility default under SF-D010, assessed independently by a read-only native context. Registration is not implementation: fresh coupled work starts after T24 eligible merge and exact-master verification.

Continue T25 local implementation and verification in a dedicated worktree while required GitHub security services for T24 draft PR37 are unavailable. This supersedes only the local start sequencing restriction in SF-D022: T24 is independently reviewed and VERIFIED locally, not merged. Create the worktree from current verified origin/master0fd6980 and fast-forward only the owned continuation branch containing exact reviewed T24 head704ef82 and immutable handoff evidence. Preserve the dependency graph, original220 acceptance, draft PR37 reviewed source, and all publication/merge gates. T25 readiness or merge requires eligible prerequisites, fresh base reconciliation, exact-head independent review, security findings classification and all required CI; no security availability exception, paid/public setting change or branch-protection bypass is inferred. Local source comparison is reversible and requires no external credentials, target authority or Oracle evidence. Use standing owner policy SF-D010 and preserve historical evidence append-only.
